title: Sales enablement: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ (2026-08)
author: Ethan Park
summary: Consolidated sales enablement reference for Redwood Inference covering positioning & messaging, competitive brief, recommended pitch deck flow, pricing guidance, exemplar case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospects.
body:
Overview

This document is the single-source sales enablement reference for customer-facing teams (AE/SDR/CS/SE) when positioning Redwood Inference in discovery and technical conversations. It combines short, repeatable messaging, a competitive brief with rebuttals, a recommended pitch-deck outline, practical pricing guidance/guardrails, two exemplar case studies with metrics, and a security FAQ for technical buyers. Use the snippets in calls, refine for the prospect, and always link to product demos and engineering contacts for deep technical discussions.

Owners and contacts
- Sales enablement owner: Ethan Park (go-to-market)
- Product SME: Priya Singh (product)
- Security SME: Lina Chen (security-and-compliance)
- SE escalation: Marco Alvarez (solutions engineering)

Audience
- AEs, SEs, SDRs, CSMs, channel partners.

Positioning (1-2 lines)
- Redwood Inference: a developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, reliable LLM serving predictable and cost-effective across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Core benefit: same API and operational tooling from prototype to production—so engineering teams avoid re-architecting as load and security requirements grow.

Key value props (elevator bullets)
- Production-grade performance: GPU-optimized runtime, latency SLOs, and autoscaling for consistent response times at scale.
- Predictable unit economics: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization guidance that cut per-token costs without sacrificing quality.
- Flexible deployment: hosted API for fast launches, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.
- Developer experience: one REST/SDK interface, built-in telemetry, and first-class rollouts (canary/A-B/fallbacks).

Messaging matrix (audience-centric)
- Engineering/Platform: "Same API & runtime from PoC to private deployments. Drop-in model pinning, automated canaries, and integrated tracing."
- Product/PM: "Lower iteration time and predictable UX—ship features quickly without inference regressions."
- Security/Compliance: "Private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC2/ISO readiness for regulated data."
- Finance/Procurement: "Transparent cost controls, reserved capacity options, and unit-cost dashboards to drive accountability."

Top objections and rebuttals
1) "We can just host models ourselves to save money."
- Rebuttal: Self-hosting has hidden TCO: engineering cycles, performance tuning, kernel/quantization expertise, and SLAs. Redwood provides proven runtime optimizations, capacity planning, and cost tools to lower TCO for product teams.
2) "What about vendor lock-in?"
- Rebuttal: We emphasize portability: model pinning, open-model catalog, and identical API semantics across hosted/dedicated/private deployments to minimize coupling.
3) "We need strict data residency."
- Rebuttal: Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and region-aware routing satisfy residency and isolation requirements; our compliance package documents evidence and controls.

Competitive brief (one-page summary)
- Competitors: Large cloud AI endpoints (Cloud-AI), LLM API providers (ModelAPICo), and inference infra vendors (SelfHostX).
- Redwood wins when customers need: consistent production latency, predictable unit economics, or private deployments with enterprise controls.
- Differentiators: unified runtime + deployment modes, cost-aware tooling (batching, caching, quant profiles), and real observability (token-level cost/latency breakdowns).
- Common competitor claims + responses:
  - Cloud-AI: "We have managed endpoints and global scale." Response: Cloud providers offer scale but often lack inference-specific optimizations (KV cache, attention kernels) and cost tooling; Redwood focuses on LLM serving economics and rollout controls.
  - ModelAPICo: "We have the best models and frictionless API." Response: Models matter, but at scale performance, cost, and private deployment options are the winning levers for product teams.
  - SelfHostX: "Our stack is open-source and cheaper." Response: Total cost of ownership and operational risk are often higher; Redwood offers managed private options and expert support to reduce ops burden.

Suggested pitch deck flow (12-18 slides)
1) Title & one-line positioning (use value props above)
2) Customer pain: inconsistent latency, runaway token costs, risky rollouts
3) Product snapshot: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (visual 3-column)
4) Runtime differentiators: batching, KV cache, quant profiles, kernel selection
5) Developer UX: single API, SDK examples (short code snippet)
6) Observability & cost controls: dashboards, per-route breakdowns
7) Enterprise controls: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SLAs
8) Pricing overview & commitment tiers (see guidance below)
9) Rollout example (canary -> A/B -> full) with metrics
10) Case study: 2-3 slides on measurable outcomes
11) Integration & timeline: PoC (2 weeks) -> Pilot (4-8 weeks) -> Prod
12) Pricing & next steps: recommended engagement model + contact

Pricing guidance (rules of thumb for reps)
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token generation + per-embedding unit). Recommend quoting monthly estimated token spend and applying standard discounts based on committed volume.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity (monthly commit) priced by GPU-equivalent throughput. Provide example: 1x reserved T4-equivalent pool suitable for ~5M tokens/day at $Xk/month (replace X with published rate from pricing portal). Use Sizing Worksheet (link to internal pricing calculator).
- Private: subscription/licensing + onboarding & support fee. Typically used by regulated customers; pricing includes packaging, on-prem installer, and support SLA.
- Discounts & negotiations: finance requires approval for >20% discount or multi-year commitments; use commercial playbook.

Template pricing snippet for early conversations
- "Based on your traffic of ~2M generated tokens/month, a hosted plan will run approximately $Y/month. For predictable latency and lower unit cost at scale, Dedicated capacity starting at $Z/month would be recommended."
(Replace Y/Z with numbers pulled from internal pricing calculator before sharing externally.)

Case studies (exemplar - redact customer names as necessary)
1) SaaS Customer (fintech) - Outcome: 62% reduction in median inference latency, 28% lower per-token cost after tuning.
- Situation: Customer moved from cloud-managed endpoints with unpredictable tail latency and high egress costs.
- Action: Onboarded to Dedicated pool, enabled KV caching for common prefixes, applied 4-bit quantization profile for non-sensitive models, and set up canary rollouts.
- Results: Median latency from 420ms -> 160ms, cost per 1k tokens reduced by 28% in first 30 days, and error rates stable (no degradation in 5% sample evals).

2) Regulated Enterprise (healthcare) - Outcome: Completed pilot in 8 weeks, passed security review, private deployment with KMS-backed key management.
- Situation: PHI-sensitive workloads required in-region processing and auditability.
- Action: Delivered Private (VPC) deployment, integrated with customer KMS, enabled long-retention audit logs, and executed canary model rollout under SE supervision.
- Results: Pilot approved for production; SLA contract signed for Dedicated + Private on an annual commit.

Security FAQ for prospects (technical buyer Q&A)
Q: How do you protect customer data during inference?
A: In hosted mode, requests are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and at rest. We offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for data isolation. Sensitive key material can be stored in customer-managed KMS/HSM. Audit logging is available for all private and Dedicated deployments.

Q: Do you train or retain customer prompts or outputs?
A: By default Redwood does not train models on customer prompts. Data retention defaults are short for hosted telemetry; for regulated customers we operate under contractually-agreed retention and deletion policies and can disable telemetry collection.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is progressing toward ISO 27001 and HIPAA readiness for specific packages. See security-and-compliance evidence pages for current artifacts.

Q: How do you handle model leakage or prompt caching concerns?
A: We segregate KV caches per-customer and enforce strict memory isolation. For Private deployments, caches never leave the customer VPC. We also provide guidance on prompt engineering to avoid accidental leakage.

Q: Can you support customer-owned keys?
A: Yes - we support customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM-backed key storage for Private and Dedicated deployments.

Q: What logging/forensics are available?
A: Audit logs cover request metadata, model version, route, and timestamps; content-level logging is configurable and can be disabled or redacted for compliance. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs via secure syslog/CloudWatch connectors.

Playbook: recommended next steps for AE/SE
1) Discovery: validate scale (tokens/day), latency targets, data residency needs, and compliance requirements. Capture sample workload.
2) Align: recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with justification and estimated costs from pricing calculator.
3) Pilot: propose 4-8 week pilot with measurable goals (latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rates).
4) Close: negotiate commit/discount via finance and attach compliance addenda if needed.

Appendix: Call scripts and one-liners
- "If you need predictable latency and a path from PoC to private deployment without re-architecting, Redwood is built for that."
- "We focus on inference economics - same API, better cost controls, and enterprise deployment options."

Document maintenance
- Review cadence: Quarterly (next review 2026-11-05)
